d1-bridges|desk|hard|lead.body: Pennsylvania will receive $410 million in federal grants to repair aging bridges, the U.S. Department of Transportation announced Wednesday. d3-overdose|castillo|hard|lead.headline: Overdose deaths fall 12 percent, but Kensington still bears a third
d3-overdose|castillo|hard|lead.deck: Philadelphia's health department reports a 12 percent drop in overdose deaths over the first nine months, with Kensington still accounting for about a third of them.
d3-overdose|castillo|hard|lead.body: Overdose deaths in Philadelphia fell 12 percent in the first nine months of the year compared with the same period last year, according to a health department report released Friday. The decline is real, but Kensington and surrounding neighborhoods still accounted for about a third of all deaths, a concentration that has not eased. The department said it will add two mobile outreach vans offering treatment referrals and overdose-reversal medication. The report does not say when the vans will begin operating in Kensington or how many people they are expected to reach.

d4-biztax|brenner|hard|lead.deck: Councilmember Teresa Vance's proposal would cost the city an estimated $22 million a year, and budget officials say the city cannot afford it.
d4-biztax|brenner|hard|lead.body: A bill to slash the business privilege tax for companies earning under $1 million a year landed on the council table Monday, and the bill's price tag is steep. Councilmember Teresa Vance, who represents part of the Northeast, introduced the measure, and her own office estimates it would cost the city $22 million a year. Vance argues the cut would help small businesses hire. Budget officials were blunt in response: the city cannot afford it while staring down a $90 million gap. The question now is who pays the difference, and how a city already short $90 million plans to fund a $22 million hole it has not yet been asked to fill.
